result.title: GLIDE: Scalable and Event-Aware Inductive Forecasting over Evolving Logistics Graphs
result.summary: Accurate forecasting of order volume at scale-effect hotspots (SEHs), spatially coherent groups of logistics flows that serve as distributed optimization units for real-time many-to-one dispatch, is a prerequisite for efficient order pooling in on-demand food delivery (OFD) platforms such as Meituan. However, real-world logistics networks present unique challenges that render standard spatiotemporal prediction model ineffective. (i) Dynamic Topology: Unlike static road networks, logistics graphs are ephemeral, with hotspot emerging and vanishing continuously; (ii) Scale--Volume Heterogeneity: Graph sizes vary from $10^2$ to $10^4$, while zero-inflated, long-tailed volumes create computational bottlenecks and bias predictions toward inactivity; and (iii) Event-Driven Disruption: Exogenous events (holidays, weather, academic calendars) induce systematic demand shifts that purely data-driven backbones cannot anticipate. In this paper, we present GLIDE, a production-ready framework that models evolving logistics graphs in a scalable latent space while adapting to heterogeneous demand regimes and event-driven shifts. GLIDE introduces a Graph-Guided Latent Aggregation mechanism, which dynamically projects varying physical subgraphs into a fixed-size, semantically stable latent space via a differentiable sparse assignment...

AI.brief_summary: 面向即时配送中动态物流图的订单量预测，提出 GLIDE 框架，用可微稀疏分配将规模各异的物理子图投影到固定大小、语义稳定的 latent 空间，并对事件驱动的需求偏移做自适应建模。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「变规模结构→定长 latent 表示」的聚合方式可能为 LVR 中固定容量 latent 工作区与长度泛化的状态压缩提供核查线索；但任务本身是时空需求预测，不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
